_schema.status: CLOSED 2026-09-17 (APPEALS-3, Fred's ruling): appeal letters cite evidence, never law. No letter path reads this table any more (verify/allowlist.py's prompt injection was removed); the twelve rows stay as the historical record of a review that was never commissioned. reviewed_by stays null on every row by design. See docs/legal-review/README.md.
_schema.what: The human-curated candidate table (design doc §5, §5a). One row = one provision counsel would actually reach for, for one denial code, in one state, for one payer type. The gates verify that a provision SAYS what the row claims and APPLIES; nothing verifies it is the RIGHT provision -- that is what curator, rationale and reviewed_by are for.
_schema.rule: A row enters a letter's allow-list ONLY when reviewed_by is set. Draft rows (reviewed_by null) are proposals: visible here, invisible to the gate. On 2026-09-14 every row is a draft, so every allow-list is empty and every letter cites nothing -- by design (§5b).

columns.state: two-letter; the practice's state. Rows for a state with no adapter cannot be reviewed into use.
columns.denial_code: CARC as the product uses it (CO-16, CO-45, CO-97, CO-4, CO-50, OA-18, PR-1)
columns.cite: the citation string exactly as the letter may print it
columns.characterisation: how the letter may characterise it (HEADING is checked against this)
columns.may_assert: what the letter may say the provision requires; every number in it must FIGURE-bind to the fetched text
columns.rationale: why this provision for this denial code, in a sentence -- the apposite-ness judgement nothing else checks

rows.characterisation: third-party payers processing claims for payment
rows.may_assert: a third-party payer must notify the provider of a material deficiency not later than fifteen days after receipt of the claim, and pay or deny a clean claim not later than thirty days after receipt (forty-five days when supporting documentation is needed)
rows.rationale: CO-16 is a missing-information denial; 3901.381 is the Ohio section that sets the deficiency-notice clock and the pay-or-deny clock for a claim on the standard form.

rows.characterisation: third-party payers processing claims for payment
rows.may_assert: a third-party payer shall pay or deny a claim not later than thirty days after receipt
rows.rationale: The deadline that governs reprocessing once the fee-schedule dispute is resolved; the contracted rate itself comes from the provider agreement, not from statute.

rows.characterisation: computation of interest on late claim payments
rows.may_assert: interest on a claim not paid when due accrues at an annual percentage rate of eighteen per cent and is paid directly to the provider
rows.rationale: An underpayment left unpaid past the 3901.381 deadline carries statutory interest; this is the section that says how much.

rows.characterisation: third-party payers processing claims for payment
rows.may_assert: a third-party payer shall pay or deny a claim not later than thirty days after receipt
rows.rationale: Ohio statute says nothing about bundling; the only Ohio obligation a CO-97 letter can state is the pay-or-deny clock on reprocessing. The coding argument rests on CPT conventions, which are not free primary law and stay generic.

rows.characterisation: third-party payers processing claims for payment
rows.may_assert: a third-party payer shall pay or deny a claim not later than thirty days after receipt
rows.rationale: As for CO-97: the modifier argument is CPT convention; the statute supplies only the clock.

rows.characterisation: external review of adverse benefit determinations
rows.may_assert: an adverse benefit determination based on medical necessity is subject to external review by an independent review organization under Ohio's external review chapter
rows.rationale: CO-50 is a medical-necessity denial; Chapter 3922 is Ohio's external-review chapter and 3922.01 is where its definitions, including adverse benefit determination, live. A reviewer should decide whether the operative request section is the better cite.

rows.characterisation: prohibition against unfair or deceptive acts in the business of insurance
rows.may_assert: no person shall engage in any trade practice defined as an unfair or deceptive act or practice in the business of insurance
rows.rationale: The general prohibition a complaint to the Department of Insurance rests on; whether a bare CO-50 without disclosed criteria reaches it is a judgement for the reviewer, not the gate.

rows.characterisation: third-party payers processing claims for payment
rows.may_assert: a third-party payer shall pay or deny a claim not later than thirty days after receipt
rows.rationale: A duplicate denial of a distinct service is a denial of a clean claim; the clock applies. Ohio statute does not define a duplicate claim.

rows.characterisation: third-party payers processing claims for payment
rows.may_assert: a third-party payer shall pay or deny a claim not later than thirty days after receipt
rows.rationale: Only appealable when the deductible was misapplied; the statute supplies the reprocessing clock and nothing about deductible accumulation, which is plan-document territory.

rows.cite: CMS Claims Processing Manual, Publication 100-04, Chapter 1, Section 80.3.2
rows.characterisation: handling of incomplete or invalid claims
rows.may_assert: an incomplete or invalid claim is returned as unprocessable rather than denied
rows.rationale: The MAC instruction that governs what a Medicare contractor does with a claim missing information.

rows.cite: NCCI Policy Manual, Chapter 1, Section D
rows.characterisation: evaluation and management services with a procedure
rows.may_assert: a significant and separately identifiable E&M service unrelated to the decision to perform a minor surgical procedure is separately reportable with modifier 25
rows.rationale: The NCCI policy that CO-97 bundling edits implement; the separately-identifiable exception is stated there.

rows.cite: CMS Claims Processing Manual, Publication 100-04, Chapter 12, Section 30.6.6
rows.characterisation: evaluation and management services during the global surgical period, modifier 25
rows.may_assert: a significant, separately identifiable evaluation and management service on the same day as a procedure is reported with modifier 25
rows.rationale: The MAC instruction on modifiers 24, 25 and 57 during the global period.
